question: Under the Maharashtra Land Revenue Code, whose permission is needed to use agricultural land for a non-agricultural purpose?
reference: The Collector's permission is required: no land used for agriculture shall be used for any non-agricultural purpose except with the permission of the Collector.

question: Up to what area can agricultural land be used for a personal residence or a micro enterprise without non-agricultural permission under the Maharashtra Land Revenue Code?
reference: No permission is necessary for personal bona fide residential use in a non-urban area, a micro enterprise, or small commercial use, occupying an area not exceeding forty square metres.

question: In which areas does the permission-free conversion under section 42(2) of the Maharashtra Land Revenue Code not apply?
reference: It does not apply in the peripheral area of a Municipal Corporation or Municipal Council, within the control line of National Highways, State Highways, District Roads or Village Roads, or in areas notified as an Eco-sensitive Zone by the Government of India.

question: महाराष्ट्र भू-राजस्व संहिता के अनुसार क्या राष्ट्रीय राजमार्ग की कंट्रोल लाइन के भीतर बिना अनुमति कृषि भूमि का गैर-कृषि उपयोग किया जा सकता है?
reference: No. The exemption from permission is not available in the area falling within the control line of National Highways, State Highways, District Roads or Village Roads.

question: How does the Maharashtra Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act protect a tenant living in a dwelling house from eviction by the landlord?
clause: Protection of tenant in actual possession
reference: Such a tenant shall not be evicted from the dwelling house (with the materials and the site) by the landlord.

question: Under the Maharashtra Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, is there a limit on the total land a person can hold as owner or tenant?
clause: Ceiling on holdings held as owner or tenant
reference: Yes. The land held by a person as owner or tenant shall not exceed the ceiling area.

question: कूळ कायद्यानुसार घरात राहणाऱ्या कुळाला जमीनमालक घरातून काढू शकतो का?
clause: Protection of tenant in actual possession
reference: नाही. अशा कुळाला त्या राहत्या घरातून (साहित्य व जागेसह) जमीनमालक काढू शकत नाही.

question: How does the Prevention of Fragmentation and Consolidation of Holdings Act define a fragment?
reference: A fragment means a plot of land of less extent than the appropriate standard area.

question: What does standard area mean under the Prevention of Fragmentation and Consolidation of Holdings Act?
reference: Standard area, for any class of land, is the area the State Government determines under section 5 as the minimum area necessary for profitable cultivation in a particular local area.

question: How are standard areas settled under section 4 of the Fragmentation and Consolidation of Holdings Act?
reference: The State Government may, after such inquiry as it deems fit, provisionally settle for any class of land in any local area the minimum area that can be cultivated.

question: What happens to fragments in the Record of Rights once a standard area is notified under the Fragmentation Act?
reference: On notification of a standard area for a local area, all fragments in that local area shall be entered as such in the Record of Rights.

question: Can a fragment of land be transferred under the Prevention of Fragmentation and Consolidation of Holdings Act?
reference: Section 7(1), on transfer and lease of fragments, provides that no person shall transfer any fragment to which the section applies.

question: क्या विखंडन निवारण अधिनियम के तहत जमीन के टुकड़े (फ्रैगमेंट) का हस्तांतरण किया जा सकता है?
reference: धारा 7(1) (फ्रैगमेंट का हस्तांतरण और पट्टा) के अनुसार कोई भी व्यक्ति उस फ्रैगमेंट का हस्तांतरण नहीं करेगा जिस पर यह धारा लागू होती है।

question: When did the Prevention of Fragmentation and Consolidation of Holdings Act receive assent?
reference: It received the assent of the Governor General on 17 January 1948, first published in the Bombay Government Gazette on 29 January 1948.

question: How can a consolidation of holdings scheme be initiated under the Fragmentation and Consolidation of Holdings Act?
reference: Under section 15 the Government may, of its own accord or on application, declare its intention to make a scheme for consolidation of holdings.

question: Under the Maharashtra Aadhaar Act 2016, can the State require Aadhaar authentication as a condition for receiving a subsidy or benefit?
reference: Yes. Under section 3 the State Government or its agency may, to establish identity as a condition for receipt of a subsidy, benefit or service, require Aadhaar authentication or proof of possession of an Aadhaar number.

question: What must be offered to a person who has not been assigned an Aadhaar number under the Maharashtra Aadhaar Act?
reference: Until an Aadhaar number is assigned, the individual shall be offered alternate and viable means of identification for delivery of the subsidy, benefit or service.

question: Within what period must the State notify the list of schemes requiring Aadhaar authentication under the Maharashtra Aadhaar Act?
reference: Within three months from the date of commencement of the Act, and thereafter from time to time.

question: When did the Maharashtra Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act come into force?
reference: It was brought into force with effect from 26 January 2017, by a notification dated 24 January 2017.

question: How does a planning authority begin preparing a development plan under the Maharashtra Regional and Town Planning Act?
reference: By a declaration of intention to prepare a development plan under section 23(1).

question: Which section of the Maharashtra Regional and Town Planning Act provides for a survey and preparation of an existing-land-use map?
reference: Section 25: provision for survey and preparation of existing-land-use map.

question: How often must a development plan be revised under the MR&TP Act?
reference: At least once in twenty years, under section 38 (revision of development plan).

question: एमआरटीपी कायद्यानुसार विकास आराखडा किती वर्षांनी सुधारित करावा लागतो?
reference: कलम 38 नुसार किमान वीस वर्षांतून एकदा विकास आराखडा सुधारित करावा लागतो.

question: Which UDCPR regulation sets the permissible FSI?
reference: Regulation 6.3, Permissible FSI.

question: Which UDCPR regulation covers net plot area and the computation of FSI?
reference: Regulation 3.9, Net Plot Area and Computation of FSI.

question: What is Basic FSI under the Unified Development Control and Promotion Regulations?
reference: Basic FSI means the floor space index permissible without levy of premium or loading of TDR.

question: Which UDCPR regulation deals with the transfer of DP sites in lieu of FSI?
reference: Regulation 3.10, Transfer of DP Sites (other than DP road) in lieu of FSI.

question: Which UDCPR regulation covers the FSI of lands affected by HEMRL or other restrictions?
reference: Regulation 6.13, FSI of Lands Affected by HEMRL or Other Restrictions.

question: What capital subsidy range does the Maharashtra Industries, Investment and Services Policy 2025 give textile units?
reference: A capital subsidy ranging from 25 to 45 per cent, provided zone-wise to individual textile units.

question: What subsidy is offered to Technical Textile Parks under the Maharashtra Industries Policy 2025?
reference: Six Technical Textile Parks; parks with ₹400–₹1000 crore investment are eligible for 55% subsidy or ₹250 crore, whichever is lower.

question: What subsidy do Mini Textile Complexes get under the Maharashtra Industries, Investment and Services Policy 2025?
reference: 18 Mini Textile Complexes; 40% subsidy on total project cost or ₹30 crore, whichever is lower.

question: What subsidy is offered for solar projects in the textile sector under the Maharashtra Industries Policy 2025?
reference: 50% subsidy for solar projects, up to ₹5 crore.

question: What investment and employment targets does the Maharashtra Industries Policy 2025 set for the textile sector?
reference: Attract ₹25,000 crore investment and create 5 lakh jobs in 5 years.

question: What is the cotton processing capacity target in the Maharashtra Industries, Investment and Services Policy 2025?
reference: Raise cotton processing capacity from 30% to 80% in 5 years.

question: What budgetary outlay does Invest Maharashtra operate with under the Maharashtra Industries Policy 2025?
reference: A budgetary outlay of ₹3,000 crore.

question: What are the investment and employment thresholds for Ultra-Mega industrial units under the Package Scheme of Incentives 2019?
clause: Table 3 — Eligibility Criteria for Mega and Ultra-mega Units
reference: Ultra-Mega Industrial Units, entire State: ₹4,000 crore investment and 4,000 direct employment.

question: What thresholds define a Mega industrial unit in A and B areas under Maharashtra's Industrial Policy 2019?
clause: Table 3 — Eligibility Criteria for Mega and Ultra-mega Units
reference: Mega Industrial Units in A & B areas: ₹1,500 crore investment and 2,000 direct employment.

question: What are the Mega unit thresholds for No Industry Districts under the Maharashtra Industrial Policy 2019?
clause: Table 3 — Eligibility Criteria for Mega and Ultra-mega Units
reference: No Industry Districts, Naxalism Affected Areas and Aspirational Districts: ₹200 crore investment and 350 direct employment.

question: What investment and employment make a Large Scale Industry in A and B areas under the 2019 Package Scheme of Incentives?
reference: A & B areas: ₹750 crore investment and 1,000 direct employment.

question: What happens to the Industrial Promotion Subsidy if a mega project does not maintain its employment criteria under the Industrial Policy 2019?
reference: If the employment criteria is not maintained for any period of the year, the Industrial Promotion Subsidy shall not be admissible for that year.
gold_snippet: Industrial Promotion Subsidy shall not be admissible

question: Within how long must the minimum direct employment be created under the Maharashtra Industrial Policy 2019?
reference: Within three years from the date of commercial production.

question: What stamp duty benefit do eligible large units get under the Package Scheme of Incentives 2019?
reference: 100 per cent stamp duty exemption within the investment period for acquiring land and for term loan purposes.

question: Which areas get electricity duty exemption for new units under the Maharashtra Industrial Policy 2019?
reference: Eligible new units in C, D, D+ areas, No Industries Districts and Naxalism affected areas, for a tenure equal to the eligibility period.

question: How is the incentive basket reduced if a unit applies late under the 2019 Package Scheme of Incentives?
reference: The basket of incentives is reduced by 5% for each year of delay in application.

question: What investment target did Maharashtra's Industrial Policy 2019 set for 2023-24?
reference: Attract investments worth INR 10 lakh crore by 2023-24.

question: How is land under de-notified SEZs on MIDC land to be developed under the Industrial Policy 2013?
reference: Lands under SEZs notified on MIDC lands shall, upon de-notification, be developed as per the Development Control Regulations (DCR).
gold_snippet: shall be developed as per the Development Control Regulations

question: How can I.T. and B.T. SEZ lands smaller than 40 hectares be developed after de-notification under the Industrial Policy 2013?
reference: They could be developed as per the prevailing IT/BT policy of the State.

question: How many acres of dedicated logistics infrastructure does the Maharashtra Logistics Policy 2024 aim to develop?
reference: More than 10,000 acres of dedicated logistics infrastructure across the state.

question: How are logistics parks classified under the Maharashtra Logistics Policy 2024?
reference: As Multi-Storeyed, Small, Large, Mega and Ultra mega logistics parks, based on scale of operations and area earmarked for logistics and related eligible activities.

question: What logistics services should a logistics park include under the Maharashtra Logistics Policy 2024?
reference: Warehousing and storage, cargo aggregation and segregation, sorting, grading, packaging, labelling, inspection, testing, quality check and distribution.
